close_reason: Dropped the .map(|v| v as &[String]) no-op coercion at event.rs:1018 and principal.rs:103. as_deref() already returns Option<&[String]>; the map was an identity. fmt/clippy/test all green.
description:
Two sites pass a properties slice through a no-op cast:

event.rs:973:
  properties.as_deref().map(|v| v as &[String])

principal.rs:83:
  event_properties.as_deref().map(|v| v as &[String])

Option<Vec<String>>::as_deref() already returns Option<&[String]>. The subsequent .map(|v| v as &[String]) coerces &[String] to &[String] — a no-op. Simply use:

  properties.as_deref()

Same byte-identical result, half the line. The redundancy might confuse a reader into thinking the cast is doing real work (changing the slice element type, perhaps?) when it isn't.

clippy::map_identity should fire on this; if it doesn't, that's because the cast expression isn't pure identity (the 'as' cast is technically a coercion, not an identity map). Either way: dead code.
title: Redundant 'as_deref().map(|v| v as &[String])' no-op cast
